description: A date field: a trigger that reads like an input and opens a <Calendar> in a <Popover>. Picking a day sets the value and closes. The shown date is formatted with Intl; the calendar carries the keyboard contract. Copy: the label names the event, not the field — "Delivery date". The placeholder shows the format the reader may type, and it is the format their locale writes.

props.name: id
props.description: Lands on the trigger, so `<Field htmlFor>` reaches it and an `ErrorSummary` row can put focus on it (see Select — same gap, same day).

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP-47 locale for the shown date + the calendar. Defaults to document lang.

props.name: invalid
props.description: A STATE, not a style: it turns the border and hands <Field> the hook it needs to read the error out as part of the field.

props.name: surface
props.description: Which surface the field sits on. On `muted` (a page/PageHeader) the border is dropped since the white fill separates it; `base` (default, a white card or form) keeps the border. Invalid + focus stay visible on both.

props.name: size
props.description: sm / md (default) / lg — matches the shared control height/padding scale.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dimmed and unpressable, but pointer events are KEPT so a Tooltip can say why. A control the reader cannot use and cannot ask about is a dead end.

example:
const [delivery, setDelivery] = useState<Date>()
const [review, setReview] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date(2026, 0, 15))

<Stack gap={6}>
  <Field label="Delivery date" htmlFor="delivery">
    <DatePicker
      id="delivery"
      label="Delivery date"
      surface="muted"
      value={delivery}
      onChange={setDelivery}
      min={new Date(2026, 0, 1)}
    />
  </Field>
  <Card>
    <Field label="Review on" htmlFor="review">
      <DatePicker id="review" label="Review on" value={review} onChange={setReview} />
    </Field>
  </Card>
</Stack>
